acceptance_criteria.criterion: Add assigns a new Guid Id and appends the connection to AppOptions.Database.Connections.
Remove(id) removes the entry and clears ActiveConnectionId when the removed id was active.
Every mutation invokes ISettingsService.SaveAsync exactly once.
The store treats the connections list immutably (no in-place list mutation that would alias the persisted snapshot).

comments.note: JsonDatabaseConnectionStore.SaveAsync mutates a local List<T> copy before creating a new AppOptions record. The ToList() call creates a new copy so the original IReadOnlyList is never aliased. The Ref<T> helper in tests is a small but effective workaround for lambda capture of mutable state in C# — acceptable for test code.

GetActiveAsync is a read-only operation returning Task.FromResult synchronously. Consider caching the connection lookup if the connections list grows large, but premature optimization — fine for expected single-digit connection counts.

summary: Reviewed 6 files (JsonDatabaseConnectionStore.cs, JsonSettingsService.cs, DatabaseConnectionOptions.cs, DatabaseOptions.cs, IDatabaseConnectionStore.cs, ISettingsService.cs). All OWASP Top 10 categories evaluated. 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Medium (plaintext password — by design), 1 Info (no mutation logging). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: MEDIUM | A02 — Cryptographic Failures | File: src/VideoIndexer.Core/Options/DatabaseConnectionOptions.cs, line 36 (Password property). DatabaseConnectionOptions.Password is persisted as cleartext in the JSON settings file on disk. The docstring acknowledges this ('stored at the user's discretion'), indicating intentional design. For a local single-user desktop tool this is a common trade-off, but it means database credentials are readable by any process with access to the settings file. Remediation (when warranted): integrate OS credential store (DPAPI on Windows via System.Security.Cryptography.ProtectedData, or Keychain on macOS) to encrypt the password at rest; or accept the design decision with clear user-facing documentation about the risk.

INFO | A09 — Security Logging & Monitoring | File: src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Settings/JsonDatabaseConnectionStore.cs. No logging is present in JsonDatabaseConnectionStore — connection additions, deletions, and active-connection changes produce no audit trail. Low severity for a desktop app, but adding ILogger calls at Debug/Information level to SaveAsync, DeleteAsync, and SetActiveAsync would improve observability and troubleshooting. Does not block approval.

INFO | A04 — Insecure Design | File: src/VideoIndexer.Core/Options/DatabaseConnectionOptions.cs. Port property accepts any integer value (no range constraint 0–65535). Validation should occur at connection-use time, not in the settings record, so this is by design. Flagged for awareness — a guard at the ViewModel/UI layer when a user enters a port value is the appropriate enforcement point.

summary: PASS with Fix-Forward. JsonDatabaseConnectionStore is clean, well-structured, and correctly implements all 5 ACs.

Fix-Forward applied: in SaveAsync, DeleteAsync, and SetActiveAsync, _settings.Current was accessed 2+ times per method. A SettingsChanged subscriber or re-entrant caller could change Current between the first read (captured into `db`) and the second read used as the with-expression base, producing a snapshot built from two different generations of state. Captured `var current = _settings.Current` once at the top of each mutation method. Non-behavioral in the current single-threaded desktop context; defensive against future concurrency.
No blocking issues found. Architecture, maintainability, best practices, and performance all meet standards.

comments.note: Fix-Forward: SaveAsync, DeleteAsync, SetActiveAsync each accessed _settings.Current more than once. Added `var current = _settings.Current` as the first statement in each mutation method and replaced all subsequent _settings.Current reads with `current`. Eliminates TOCTOU exposure where a SettingsChanged event handler that calls back into the store (re-entrant) or a concurrent SaveAsync could change Current between the two reads, causing the with-expression to merge two different snapshot generations. Non-behavioral under current single-threaded UI dispatch, but defensive against re-entrant SettingsChanged subscribers and any future background refresh of ISettingsService.

[documentation-forward] IDatabaseConnectionStore.SaveAsync interface summary says 'Adds or replaces a connection entry identified by Id' but does not document the auto-Guid assignment behaviour: when Id == Guid.Empty the implementation assigns a new Guid before persisting. DatabaseConnectionOptions.Id defaults to Guid.NewGuid() so callers constructing a record normally will never trigger this path unintentionally, but callers who explicitly want an insert-with-server-assigned-id should know to pass Id = Guid.Empty. Add a <remarks> block to the interface method doc describing this contract.

GetAllAsync and GetActiveAsync use Task.FromResult for synchronous value returns. This is intentional and appropriate for the expected single-digit connection-list size, consistent with the Developer's own observation. No action required — flagged for awareness only.
